changelog: An update no longer stops a request with a fatal error. On the demo, the minute 1.12.0 replaced 1.11.3, one request to Dashboard → Updates died on plugins_loaded with "class CreativeBranding\Tracking\Plugin not found": it had loaded the plugin just before WordPress moved the 1.11.3 folder out, and reached plugins_loaded while the folder was missing, with an autoloader pointing at files no longer there. (The update itself runs in another request, and requests arriving during it get WordPress's maintenance page; only one already under way can meet the missing folder.) The main file now hooks its own functions, on the same hooks at the same priorities, and each runs the plugin only once its files are on disk; otherwise that request goes on without it, quietly, and the next has the new files. The same guard covers the updater, activation, deactivation and the Plugins row's links. A request still running the version being replaced is the one at risk, so updates from 1.12.1 on are covered; the update from 1.12.0 to 1.12.1 can still log this once.
tracking-page-items.php: Plugin Check's warning on the item photo is suppressed inline; wp_get_attachment_image() escapes its own markup.
tools/update-race.sh updates a throwaway site while requests keep arriving and reports any fatal error, for checking a release before it goes out.
